technique_name: Compare and contrast Depth-First Search (DFS) and Breadth-First Search (BFS).
description: Depth-First Search (DFS) is a search strategy that starts by exploring one path in depth before backtracking and exploring alternative paths. On the other hand, Breadth-First Search (BFS) starts at the root node and scans every adjacent node before visiting the next node in a level order manner. DFS is typically used for finding a certain element in a graph, while BFS is often used for traversing the entire tree or graph and for finding the shortest path from one node to another.
